title: Grateful Dead Live at Betty Nelson's Organic Raspberry Farm on 1968-09-02
lineage: SBD > Master Reel (Three half-inch four track reels, recorded on Ampex 440) > Master Dat (Sony R500) > SEK'D Prodif Plus > Samplitude v7.02 Professional > Cool Edit Pro v2.0 > SHN

ai_review.summary: Clean soundboard capture of a high‑energy ’68 set highlighted by a smoking Dark Star, The Eleven and the Alligator→Caution pairing.
ai_review.review: The Miller source delivers a generally crisp and well‑balanced soundboard recording, despite occasional vocal level quirks and a few track‑listing mishaps. Musically the show shines with powerhouse jams – Dark Star, St. Stephen, The Eleven, Alligator, Caution and an intense Other One suite – delivering the high‑octane energy Dead fans associate with late‑summer ’68 performances.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is 4.25; most comments praise the performance and note clean sound, with only minor technical complaints, indicating a strong show captured on a good‑quality soundboard.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally super‑clean balance and crisp presence; occasional vocal level issues, drums emphasized in mix, sporadic mic turn‑offs and glitches; track‑listing metadata is a mess but does not affect audio fidelity.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Despite a chaotic track‑listing, the concert flows powerfully with back‑to‑back jam sequences (Dark Star→St. Stephen→The Eleven, Alligator→Caution) that keep the momentum high.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar work is highlighted as "flying" through extended jams, especially on Dark Star and The Eleven.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass provides solid rhythmic shifts and underpins the jam sections; a few reviewers note his changes in key during transitions.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drums are prominent in the mix (sometimes overly loud) and drive the energy on Caution and other high‑octane moments.
